steps.text: Cut potatoes, onions, and celery into fairly large chunks; place in the bottom of a slow cooker along with baby carrots. Place roast on top of vegetables. Place 3 bouillon cubes randomly on top of the roast and pour in 1/2 cup water.
Cover and cook on Low for 6 to 8 hours or on High for 4 to 5 hours. An instant-read thermometer inserted in the thickest part of the roast should read 145 degrees F (65 degrees C).
Transfer roast to a platter. Remove vegetables using a slotted spoon and arrange them around the roast.

raw_recipe.headline: Easiest Pot Roast Ever
raw_recipe.description: Make the best pot roast with this easy slow cooker recipe! The roast cooks on top of vegetables, resulting in tender meat and veggies for a comforting meal.

video.description: Easy one pot meal that has delicious results! Vegetables like potatoes, carrots, and celery cook along with pot roast and beef bouillon for the ultimate satisfying meal!

review.reviewBody: I used this recipe for my first roast and have used it religiously since. My only advice would be to watch your cooking time. My roasts have always been done between 5-6 hours (on low) and they come out very tender. Overall, a very easy and tasteful recipe.

I don't know what some of these people are talking about - this was a great roast! You may want to add some more spices, but that's not rocket science. I added a litte bit of garlic, a sprinkle of garlic salt, ground pepper and extra onion flakes. My boyfriend and I loved it - it was a nice brown color, and the aroma filled the house when I came home. I will be using this recipe over and over.

I do it about the same in a roast pan in the oven, at 335 for around four hours. Instead of Boulion cubes, I use beef Stock and end up basically with the same results.. I'll try it in the slow cooker, but it seems to me it should require a bit more time? It isa favorite of mine and was for my late wife. Usually once a week. Now when I can entice company I usually serve that if on a Sunday. Why on a Sunday? Just old habits are hard to break. Bon Appetit
This recipe makes an excellent dish. I added about a tablespoon of Worcestershire sauce and about 3 tablespoons of ketchup. (That’s MY secret ingredient). Comes out tasting fantastic every time.

This needs garlic, onions, rosemary and thyme..salt, pepper, mushrooms.. Otherwise it's way too bland.. I'm a retired chef..never would use this recipe. You must sear the meat too. Will need more liquid for 3 to 4 pound roast. About 1 cup.

I'm giving this a 5 because I love how it is both a simple and effective recipe. It is easy to modify to your taste (and worth modifying to add some taste).

I used a 2.5 lb roast. I cooked it on high for 4 hours using slow cooker mode in an instant pot (I was in a pinch). 

It turned out great, though the meat was a bit tough due to my very short cooking time; same thing for the vegetables. 

I used the instant pot high pressure for 5 minutes more - this solved the overly firm vegetable problem.

After shredding the meat I added it back to the pot to hang in the juices, the meat was amazing after that!... still recommending a longer cook time if possible though.

The recipe lacks flavor, and I think that is pretty obvious in the ingredient list... To give this more of a german flare, I added mustard and sliced up some small whole dill pickles. I highly recommend this! However, if you season with just salt and pepper, I'm sure that will satisfy those with a simple palate.

Alright, this is a great kickoff start recipe. Here are the changes I made, keep in mind that I used a 7 qt Crockpot... 1. Ditched the celery and added more carrots and potatoes 2. I used a 3.5 lb chuck roast which I pre-seasoned with salt, pepper, onion and garlic powder. I then seared all sides of the beef for a couple of minutes each side. 3. Placed most of the veggies on the bottom of the pot, put the meat on top and used the rest of the veg to fill in around the sides. 4. In addition to the bouillon cubes, I added a packet of Lipton onion soup mix on top of the whole shebang. I cooked mine an additional 2.25 hours because I first set the pot to warm instead of low (Facepalm) I pushed the unmelted bouillon cubes into the juice about halfway through the cook to get all that beefy goodness to the rest of the party. After an unintentional 10.5 hours of cook time, I had a savory, fall apart pot roast that had more than enough juice to make some gravy by thickening with some cornflower slurry.

Used a 5 lb. roast, and rubbed it with salt, pepper and garlic powder. I dredged it in flour and then seared it in olive oil. After reading the reviews, I added 2t of garlic, a couple shakes of ground coriander, and then cooked it for 10 hours on low. No knife required!

Absolutely 100% recommend this recipe! SO TENDER! So simple! I had just a little over 3 Lbs and it cooked on low in about 4 hours. I did add Garlic Powder, Onion Powder, and dried thyme. Rubbed both sides down then floured and seared on each side for about 3 minutes on med high in a skillet before placing on top of large chopped carrots. Used powdered bouillon and mixed it with hot water and poured over the top (That's just our go to method) Thank you for sharing! My last few roasts have been like shoe leather!
I add 1 package of Beef Onion soup mix and 1/2 cup of catsup. A handful of brown sugar. Also HATE fake baby carrots so i just buy 3------------4 loose big carrots and cut them up

I used a lean, boneless beef shoulder roast, browned first on stove top, added a tbsp of Worcestershire sauce, 2 tsp of chopped garlic, and a tsp of dried basil. Added 3 cups of bone beef broth and the boullion with the water. Browning first does take away from being easy, but it's a step I've learned to take for best flavor, especially with a leaner cut of meat. The seasonings are an easy add in. And, we like a lot of gravy, so added extra liquid. Cooked on high for 3 hours, low for another 3. Yum!
Meat turned out tough and inedible. Vegetables were still hard after cooking time.

This was awful. The recipe went against everything I know about making a roast. SEAR the roast. Mix the bouillon and have more water. The roast was done and tough - veggies were raw. Had to dump It back in with two cups of water on high to get an edible meal.

The only thing I did was, take the veggies out as they were getting done to fast on the bottom. My bad as I cut them to small. And added 4-5 garlic cloves. Then I put the roast back in and the veggies on the top. I did take the broth and make gravy. It was delicious 😋 I will use this recipe to make again.
Meat came out too dry. I added salt and cut up a few shallots. I would not use this recipe again.

This is great! I did season the roast with salt, pepper, garlic powder and thyme. Then added about 2 teaspoons of Worcestershire sauce as someone had recommended. Love it! It doesn't really make a gravy but the sauce is very tasty.
Added some garlic. Browned the meat in a cast iron skillet.
Easy, works well if you add a packet of instant french onion soup mix as well. The aroma of this recipe is wonderful

I’ve tried a dozen recipes and mixes and hands down this is the simplest best tasting recipe I’ve tried for sure! I tweak it a little by adding a generous sprinkle of garlic powder and thyme. My family cleans out the pot before nights end every time!
This was easy! I seared the roast, and added garlic, garlic powder, fresh cracked black pepper, seasoning salt and onion soup mix. Superb! A new family favorite!
